newsitem.title: USA: Micron CEO says Utah plans still on hold.
newsitem.headline: Micron CEO says Utah plans still on hold.

text.p: Micron Technology Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Steve Appleton said Wednesday the company will open its new Lehi, Utah, plant only when the market demands it, and not anytime in the next year.

Appleton noted in a presentation to a Piper Jaffray investors conference that prices for the DRAM memory chips used in personal computers and other devices have risen 50 percent from depressed levels in the past several weeks but said "we would have to see that continue" before making any decision about the plant near Salt Lake City.
Micron has spent about $600 million developing the 2.2 million-square-foot facility but put it on hold indefinitely when chip prices collapsed.
Appleton said the plant, which has yet to be equipped, would not be opened in the next six to 12 months, but after that the plant could be opened depending on market conditions.

Appleton declined to predict whether DRAM prices would stabilize, but he said the company continues to operate at 100 percent capacity and is likely to increase its share of the world memory market to 10 percent by the end of the year from 7 percent currently.
"Even though DRAM prices have fluctuated, we're able to make money," he said. "We do things every down cycle that make us a much better company."
Appleton said he did not expect 64-megabit memory chips to be produced in significant volume for another two years, leaving the current-generation 16-megabit chips to be dominant.
And he said he did not expect chip manufacturers to switch to 12-inch wafers from the current-generation 8-inch "in this century," saying technical and financial hurdles were too daunting.
